newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat stays strong, puzzles brokers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat stays strong, puzzles brokers.

text.p: Australian wheat futures stayed firm on Friday, out of line with Chicago, the local cash price and the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) pool prices.
Near-term March 1997 sold 25 lots A$1.50 higher at A$169.00 a tonne, highlighting a market anomaly, brokers said.

The deal, through sales by Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd to Bain Refco Commodities Ltd, was a "good sell", a broker said. Brokers, who asked that not be named, said GrainCorp charges for deliveries into and out of the futures system brought real returns back significantly.
A A$165.00 bid in the cash market was not equivalent to a A$165.00 bid on futures, which would net out to an equivalent A$159.00 bid on cash, they said.
Wheat could have been bought more cheaply on the cash market on Friday than in the March 1997 futures transaction, they said.
The AWB pool price of A$188.00 a tonne was helping prop the futures market up, but this did not fully explain current prices, they said.
The AWB pool price was equivalent only to about A$163.00 in futures, they said.
Export prices by the AWB involved charges of about A$10.00 a tonne which reduced a A$195.00 export price to a net return of A$185.00, they said.
The market had brokers perplexed and was probably due for a slight tumble, Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd also said.
If Chicago went any lower SFE wheat should break major support, he said.
